components: small closed head flowing into a deep leftward bowl
strokeOrder: loop counterclockwise around the small closed head
continue down and left through the deep bowl without lifting
lift once, then place the upper-right dot
lift again, then place the upper-left dot

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, ق demonstration at 02:14–02:18 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ق body-first: loop counterclockwise around the small closed head, continue down and left through the deep bowl without lifting, then lift for the upper-right dot and lift again for the upper-left dot. Contextual joins shorten the bowl; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline and records Persian-scoped provenance rather than borrowing the independently verified Arabic or Urdu ق sources.

notes: Qāf is commonly pronounced like gheyn غ in modern Persian, though q remains in some dialects and loanword conventions.
